Each year at this season we are commanded to sit at the Seder Table to do anything and everything to experience the horror of slavery and then the awe-filled nature of redemption. This year, how can we commemorate the redemptive story of Pesach when 59 souls are still in literal bondage, shackled in the Gaza tunnels of terror?
 
All of us are shackled in one form or another; and all of us in this season of freedom have the potential to be free. Let us make room at our tables for anyone who needs to join us to be physically and spiritually sustained. 
 
Rachel Goldberg-Polin (mother of the murdered American-Israeli hostage, Hersh Goldberg-Polin) suggests that this year we add a lemon on our Seder plates to remind us the bitter taste of this season and to continue to do everything we can to #BRING THEM HOME!

Chag Pesach Sameach

note_tweet.text: I’m devastated by news of the deaths of six hostages in Gaza, including an American, Hersh Goldberg-Polin. May their memories be a blessing. I was so moved by Hersh’s parents’ remarks last month at the Democratic National Convention. Jon Polin and Rachel Goldberg-Polin’s courage and invincible love for their son have shone throughout their terrible ordeal. They and other hostage families have turned pain into purpose, advocacy into activism, to get the hostages released and bring an end to this conflict. My heart and my prayers are with these families during this time of immense pain and grief.
